name: AdenNet (Aden ISP / network operations centre)
developer: AdenNet (state-backed ISP of the internationally recognized government)
notes: AdenNet is an ISP created in June 2018 by the internationally recognized (Hadi-era) government as an alternative to the Houthi-controlled YemenNet, headquartered in Aden and a RIPE member with its own network infrastructure in the city. It operates network/gateway and hosting infrastructure rather than a public commercial colocation datacenter; no public MW capacity found.

name: Aden Submarine Cable Landing Station
notes: Aden is one of Yemen's three subsea cable landing points (per GeoCables, served by systems including Aden-Djibouti, Africa-1 and AAE-1). This is international telecom/connectivity infrastructure, not a commercial datacenter; no public MW capacity found.

name: Al Hudaydah Submarine Cable Landing Station (FALCON / SeaMeWe-5)
notes: The FALCON and SeaMeWe-5 submarine cables land at Al Hudaydah (Western Coast governorate), operated by TeleYemen in Houthi-controlled territory; the coastal telecom station/infrastructure has been repeatedly disrupted and was hit by a Saudi-led coalition strike that caused nationwide internet outages (May 2025, per Al Mayadeen/Ahram). This is telecom gateway infrastructure rather than a commercial datacenter; no public MW capacity found.
